item.title: (Seeking Greenlight) Aquí Hubo Escena
item.description: Memetic agent that affects songs. you either get a positive or a negative effect based on your perception of said song.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes.

Page Type: SCP Article.

Page Layout: Looking to use a format similar to those of SCP-4028, SCP-3020 and SCP-3031. Audio files if possible.

Elevator Pitch: A memetic agent starts spreading across finished musical compositions. Depending on the fame, the listener's perception and the themes the piece touches, this agent can cause all sorts of benefitial or detrimental changes on a person's body and psyche. Although the agent starts propagating on niche music spheres, it eventually reaches mainstream hits.

Central Narrative: Trough different evidence we learn about our PoI, an anomalous individual who was heavily involved in his country's music scene. In naive attempt to improve his situation and the one of his fellow companions, he ends up risking up the veil and getting the community he so much loved killed (both metaphorically and literally). After barely surviving lynching and escaping persecution, he releases the memetic agent with ambiguous motivations.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Aside from the fact this skip deals with a not so explored topic, this entry has the intent of confronting the Foundation with a fundamental dilemma: is it really better to live on your knees than to die on your feet? Is the Foundation really willing to declare a war on artistic expression for the greater good?.

Additional Notes: It's Intended to be a connection between our PoI and the GoI "Deer College", this may change in the future.

item.title: (Seeking Greenlights): Lullaby lady
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror

Elevator Pitch: An entity that resembles a female corpse that puts children under the age of 8 to coma. The entity hunts families with a child under the age of 8. It mysteriously crawls out of closets or drawers inside the victim's house at approximately 1~2 o'clock midnight. Then proceeds to sing a
"Lullaby". The lullaby affects children to wake up from their sleep immediately, but gives a counter effect to adults which puts them to deeper sleep. The child(victim) who lacks a guardian is held firmly by the entity, unable to resist. After the lullaby is over, the entity kisses the victim's forehead which makes the victim fall in a coma. The entity then disappears from the house only leaving a fowl, garlic scent.

Central Narrative:The article is narrated based on a interview between Scp agent "Joshua" and Robert, the only victim known to recover from the coma. The interview provides gruesome description
of the entity itself and events that happen inside of the coma.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: All victims in the state of coma are to be euthanized for it is the most ethical treatment the Foundation can provide. Also, the containment procedures involves animal sacrifices, torment and more unethical procedures which gives the reader curiosity of the Scp and it's powers.

Additional Notes:Thank you so much for reading and I really hope to see reviews!!

item.content:encoded:

Elevator Pitch: A sentient fountain that doesn't want to be played in or climbed on creates hydrophobia-inducing water.

Central Narrative: School-kids on their senior year start spreading a local legend among their younger peers and other people to not to interact with a certain fountain. One day, a pipe of the fountain is burst by the fountain, spreading a town’s water supply, creating a hydrophobic town.

Additional Notes: This is an old idea that already has a draft, as it was liked by many reviewers back when it was first made, both in IRC chatrooms and forum posts. item.title: Dionysus Asylum
item.description: they're here to help (whether you like it or not).
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: an insane asylum with anomalous properties that helps people with their mental issues and is often used by the foundation to contain entities that aren't mentally stable.

Central Narrative: the article mostly focuses on excerpts from a journal written by a foundation MTF agent, who was held captive by the Asylum because he suffered from PTSD after an encounter with another dangerous anomaly. the journals talk about how the agents experience within the asylum, as well as encounters with other patients, most of which happen to have anomalous properties. Eventually the agent begins to comply with the treatment and is soon released from the asylum.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: the asylum possesses multiple anomalous items such as straitjackets that induce drowsiness on anyone who wears them. the Asylums staff are completely invisible except for their brains and nervous systems, and it's implied they're all part of some kind of hive mind. The asylum itself also possesses anomalous properties, such as appearing like an abandoned building to anyone who hasn't been through/is suffering from psychological trauma or mental illnesses. Despite keeping most of it's patients there against their will, the Asylum really does just want to help people.

Additional Notes:I think given the nature of this SCP and how the foundation uses it it'd probably be a Thaumiel but I'm not entirely sure. I also considered the asylum being immune to reality warping but I'm not too sure about that either.

item.title: Echos eines Hoffest
item.description: A city returns to medieval times for a day. Foundation intervenes and it becomes permanent.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): History

Page Layout (Optional): Video logs, interviews, document references and incident logs to be included.

Elevator Pitch: The city of Mainz (Germany) gathers annually during the Pentecost day for a party in which the citizens anomalously change their behaviour as if they were in the 12th century for a day. After an incident, the Foundation intervenes only to provoke this change to become permanent.

Central Narrative: During the Pentecost day in Mainz, its citizens celebrate the festivity in a nearby location, where upon access they show an altered behaviour proper of the European nobility in the 12th century, such as a firm code of honour; and participate in joust tournaments. By the following day, citizens involved have no related memories.

+ Show
- Hide

This activity went under the radar of the Foundation until a Turkish attendant was found dead after one of these events with the words "Deus Vult" engraved on his chest. The following year, Foundation found out about these effects with on-site live-recordings. Identifying a potential assault similar to the previous year, a task force bursts into the gathering, disbanding all attendants. This time affected individuals keep their memories and the behaviour displayed during this event. Chaos ensues due to the cultural clash with modern Germany.

The next Pentecost day, affected population gathers again, live-recordings showing that the activities performed are exactly the same as in the previous year. Once the celebration finishes, all attendants return to the normal behaviour. Foundation decides not to interrupt this event, but stops population from attending by fencing the site. Instead, attendants move to nearby Ingelheim, where anomalous natural catastrophes result in hundreds of casualties. The Foundation allows the event to occur at the usual location, however impeding the attendance to vulnerable individuals.

Recording logs interview seemingly a monk, who seems to be responsible of these events. Back in 1184, Kaiser Barbarossa hosted a huge fest in that same location. By law, Konrad was to be seated by the Kaiser during the ceremonies, however he was substituted in a political move by the Archbishop of Cologne. Resentful, he condemned the dishonour, ensuring that that day would be repeated over and over until the Kaiser rectified his mistake.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: This is a story about timely cultural clash, by bringing a huge population from the past to the current days. It is also a story about resentment and, literally, holding a grudge.

Additional Notes: Based on the 1184 Mainzer Hoftag. Kaiser Barbarossa might be SCP-125-DE.

item.content:encoded:

Users will continue to float until they either hit a ceiling or the oil gets washed off. Upon hitting a ceiling or a limit, the user's oil will continue to rise until it is off the user, where it'll then fall. The user will too fall due to the oil being removed.

Central Narrative: SCP-XXXX causes user's to controllably levitate upwards, people who consume SCP-XXXX will continually float upwards until they hit a ceiling. If the user continues to float upwards, they will eventually extricate it outwards, causing the user and the extrication to fall. If people who have consumed SCP-XXXX hit a limiter or a ceiling, they will be pulled up forcefully until their organs containing the oil rupture out of the consumer. causing the user to fall.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: SCP-XXXX is seemingly safe, but due to the container continuing to fill it's environment, it could cause the end of our known universe.

Additional Notes: It's a pretty basic SAFE article.

item.title: Storm of crows
item.description: abnormal number of crows migrate directly to the town
item.content:encoded:
SCP-XXXX is an anomalous phenomenon where an abnormal number of crows migrate directly to the town, even if it off-tracks their intended migration path.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

thanks zyn!

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: SCP-XXXX is a phenomenon where an abnormal number of crows migrate directly to the town, even if it off-tracks their intended migration path.

More
Not more

The highest amount of crows in the town was 84,784.

When a house in the town is damaged, it will start to heal itself, although minor damages take less time to heal. Damages won't be healed as an identical version of the house such as doors leading to nothing, rooms or objects with an irregular shape, etc.

A unique crow will be "assigned" to a specific house. These crows are distinguishable by their single white feather. These crows will interact with the occupants of the homes.

The foundation discovered that when a crow is killed, the house's self-repairing is assigned to stops entirely.

Central Narrative: The narrative is presented in a personal journal belonging to a young teenage girl named Sahra.

more
not more

Their crow comes to their house. He's Chip because he brought a chip as a gift.

The large and irregular migration of crows to the town is detected by the locals. The town tries to find a way to scare off the crows. But it doesn't work, as every time one crow leaves, more come in.

Sarah's dad one day breaks a door hinge while slamming a door shut. He later calls one of his friends to help fix it when he gets back home, but it's fixed when they return home.

Soon the crows outnumber the town's population 31:1.

Everyone tries to scare off the crows. They use fireworks, predators, big hunting, but none of them work because every time one goes away, more come to replace it. Soon the crow's number in the thousands.

A car crashes into Sarah's house and kills chip. The damaged part attempts to repair and starts to start to expand and use wrong materials. The crow's brain went on overdrive before dying. This was when the foundation was informed.

The foundation came, amnesticize everybody, and found Sarah's journal.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: An article with a light story isn't as common as Lovecraftian horror and Apollyon class SCPs.

Additional Notes: Sarah and her family were in the first instance of SCP-XXXX which is why the foundation hadn't known about the anomaly. also had to put the bare minimum in the narrative because of the word limit.

item.title: De Facto
item.description: An octopus that exploits laws of reality to actively shape the environment however it sees fit.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes
Page Type: SCP Article
Genre: Horror

Elevator Pitch: De Facto is an intangible entity that can descend upon any location and transmute it to develop anomalous properties. It presents cephalopodic features and primarily resides outside of our reality, traveling freely along or through any surface and molding the environment into its personal hunting grounds.

Central Narrative:
+ Show
Hide Section

This creature was originally a rare variant of octopi possessing intelligence that far surpasses humans held in a secret underground marine biology laboratory. It preferred behavior often associated with its species, though can devise incredibly elaborate traps for anything it considers its prey, and adapts to immediate surroundings astonishingly fast. Its kind has been critically endangered due to human pollution and influence and retained a grudge over transgressions of its captors.

However, it eventually learned how it could adapt into reality itself and extend beyond the third dimension. It turned the entire containment facility into its personal den, transmuting the walls with an ink-coated rocky surface, restructuring the layout entirely as a system of dugouts and labyrinthian corridors, and filling various areas in an oily, repugnant ooze. Its now-countless tendrils sprawled visibly along the wall surfaces like projections, with all attempts to interfere with them showing no effect on the creature. Unnatural and anomalous phenomenon began to sprout in the twisted den: coral discharging suspended bubbles of ooze, manmade objects now malleably autonomous and extremely hostile to humans, and unspeakably horrific marine life that freely live and move through the air as if it was water.

The octopus started cornering each member of the facility’s personnel separately from each other, torturing them with whatever sadistic and anomalous means it could fabricate inside the burrows of its new home. Eventually, one by one each researcher would observe a large contorted beak emerge from the ink-black walls and gruesomely devour them, leaving enough space in the walls for everyone to hear sounds of their coworkers’ screams echo through the halls. It takes its leave when it’s finished, retracting its tentacles and ascending to the surface in search for more prey.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The creature practically infects any area with its anomalous properties, permanently transforming any building or structure into a waking nightmare.

Tags: adaptable, amorphous, animal, building, carnivorous, cephalopodic, hostile, intangible, keter, predatory, sentient, transfiguration

item.title: The Drag Strip Phantom / The Black Magnum [Seeking Greenlight]
item.content:encoded:
An SCP heavily and very directly inspired by Christine, The Wraith, Death Proof and SLR:Redline.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Mystery/Thriller

Page Layout (Optional): Standard description and event chronology as well as mission reports and test logs

Elevator Pitch: The phantom of a car that manifests itself on lonely stretches of desert road at night to challenge high-performance passer-by cars to a drag race. Original manifestation is 1970 Camaro, however the list will expand later.

Central Narrative: A rumor spreads in a small town in Colorado about a mysterious "ghost car", originating from a local drag racing enthusiast. According to the legend, the racer is overtaken by a dragster and the road eventually leads into a foggy, abandoned drag strip - with a stoplight and everything. The Foundation takes note after several others report the same occurence and dispatches a team to study the anomaly up-close and personal ("prodding" the car during manifestations and exploring the strip dimension), as well as launching an investigation into the car's possible origins.

+ show block
– hide block

At one point, a GoI destroys it (no clue which one yet); after which, basically, Christine happens: Someone finds a junk 1970 Camaro, and with maniacal passion restores it, builds it and, in the end, crashes it violently, dying - thus causing the phantom to be "reborn". Following rediscovery the Foundation tries to relocate it to the most discreet stretch of blacktop possible and keep it happy by regularly setting up drag races.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The mystery surrounding the car itself: Is it sentient, is it dangerous, what is the drag strip, is/was it a real place, where does the car come from, is there anyone driving it, what is its driving force etc. etc.

Additional Notes: The drag strip is a separate dimension that flat-out disables digital and some complex electronic devices./Cars cannot leave the dimension unless they engage in the race or get totaled./Anyone who dies on the strip in a car becomes another manifestation./The phantoms are free to switch or modify their vessels - however can only do so by leaving their old vessel in the real world or possessing somebody to do it, respectively./The phantom sustains itself off of life energy gained in the final stage of its "rebirth"./Each phantom is sentient and has a memory beyond its current vessel./The SCP can manifest at will anytime between sunset and dawn./It is not bound to any road in particular and can move at any time.

item.title: [Need Greenlight] The bipolar statue
item.description: Also, has this been done before? [thread locked, repeat]
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes
Page Type: SCP article
Elevator Pitch:A simple bronze statue, 3 meters in height, with an emotionless, nondescript face. The statue, each day of the year, produces an object that is laid at the feet of the statue. This object can vary, from a blank book, a briefcase of money, or a gun. The way this object is used depends on the weather, therefore creating an infinite amount of possibilities for what could happen, with global warming and greenhouse gases. The statue also sometimes goes into a "bad" mood, with the item that is produced being used against the person picking it up, for example, a handgun produced at the feet of the statue could have the safety off and be fully loaded, giving a chance for the person picking it up to shoot themselves if they are not careful.
Central Narrative: Not sure what they are talking about, so… none?
Hook/attention grabber: Its a statue that can give you a "gift" or kill you.
